question: What is the role of chemically inactive gases in a light bulb?

options.text: To reduce the bulb's light output
To prolong the life of the filament

solution:
The correct answer is __To prolong the life of the filament**(Option 3)**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Chemically inactive gases__ are also known as inert gases.
 
• Inert gases such as argon or nitrogen are filled inside light bulbs.
 
• The role of these gases is to reduce the evaporation of the filament, thus prolonging its life.
 
• Without these gases, the filament would burn out quickly due to oxidation at high temperatures.
 
• Inert gases also prevent the glass bulb from blackening due to tungsten vapor deposition.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Filament Materials:**
 
 
• Tungsten is the most commonly used filament material due to its high melting point and durability.
 
• It can withstand high temperatures required to produce visible light.
 
 
 
• **Halogen Bulbs:**
 
 
• In halogen light bulbs, a small amount of halogen gas is added, which increases the efficiency and lifespan of the bulb.
 
• This prevents the tungsten filament from thinning and allows it to operate at higher temperatures.
